summary: The corrected partial-restart experiment executed (receipt 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837): with two of three voters restarted under RestoreCommittedLogs, the untouched configured voter leads with the configuration-less nodes' votes (servers [0,0,3]), and once it stops the two remaining live, fully up-to-date voters (log index 13 on both) cannot elect a leader in six seconds — comparison violated at index 1 — while the no-flag control re-elects (holds, index 3). The interpretation now cites all five retained receipts and states the cluster-wide progress loss as the live quorum of a majority failing to elect, with the build-failure receipt retained but excluded as evidence. For the remaining safety question I recorded a source-backed reachability analysis: a voter missing the silently created {A,B,E} entry is always strictly behind and cannot win over a voter holding it, so a disjoint-majority election requires the two-server change to commit without one old voter — reachable because the new configuration is installed into commitment on append, allowing A plus a promoted caught-up nonvoter E to commit while B is partitioned — and the open test is whether the old majority {B,C} can then elect a higher-term leader that truncates A's committed entry X when the partition heals. That discriminator is registered for the next probe.
